A: Axial FLAIR MRI panel from a patient with MSUD shows subtle hyperintense signal in the dorsal brainstem/cerebellar white matter as described in the caption; an arrow annotates the region. B: Axial DWI MRI panel demonstrates restricted diffusion in the dorsal brainstem and cerebellar white matter, characteristic of MSUD. C: Axial FLAIR MRI panel shows subtle hyperintense signal in the cerebellar white matter/vermis in a patient with MSUD; an arrow annotates the region. D: Axial DWI MRI panel demonstrates restricted diffusion in the cerebellar white matter/vermis and dorsal brainstem, consistent with MSUD.

A: Panel A is an axial brain MRI from a patient with maple syrup urine disease, showing FLAIR hyperintense signal in the bilateral globus pallidum and other characteristic locations. The caption supports MSUD-related neuroimaging involvement; thalamus, genu, and posterior limb/internal capsule findings are not fully covered by the allowed vocabulary. B: Panel B is an axial diffusion-weighted brain MRI from a patient with maple syrup urine disease, showing diffusion restriction in the bilateral globus pallidum and posterior limb of the internal capsule, classic for MSUD encephalopathy. Thalamic and genu involvement are also described but lack matching vocabulary keys.

in_text_mentions: ein restriction. The next day of admission, he had a headache and transient abnormal hand movements. A CT scan of the brain showed diffuse cerebral edema causing cerebellar tonsillar herniation (Fig. 1: A and B). He remained fully conscious with no focal neurological signs. Plasma leucine was 1300, isoleucine 237 and valine 271 µmol/L. He was shifted to the ICU and received continuous renal replacement therapy (CRRT) for 48 h until leucine levels were reduced to 400 µmol/L. Conservative management continued with hypertonic saline infusion, high-calorie intake, BCAA-free formula and valine and

µmol/L in the following few months. CT brain scan after 12 weeks of the initial presentation showed further improvement of cerebral edema and resolution of cerebellar tonsillar herniation. However, his vision remained poor, which justified magnetic resonance imaging (MRI; Fig. 1C) demonstrating persistent brain edema in a distribution compatible with MSUD extending to the optic tracts. The optic nerves were mildly atrophic, with a mildly abnormal signal in the optic chiasma. His dietary compliance, which initially improved for a few months after discharge from the hospital, gradually worsened.
